# Module map

[Project entry](../../README.md) · [Documentation](../README.md) · [Agent guide](../agents/README.md)

Find a module's purpose, source, scope, recorded progress and next review. This map covers **27 module roots**: 23 pnpm workspace packages, 1 extension without package.json, and 3 nested support packages. Source review: **2026-09-28**.

**Start with the website:** [Storefront domains](storefront/README.md) groups 72 library directories and 77 route families by purpose.

**Current boundary:** [New paid commerce is retired](../../apps/storefront/docs/commercial-retirement.md). Retained source can support existing agreements, a preview, a paused feature or historical compatibility. Presence in this map is not a release or service-health claim.

## How the pieces connect

The storefront is the main visitor and operator application. Wholesale retains its research and existing-order responsibilities. RewardsPro owns its current loyalty platform and extensions; RewardsPro API is a separate backend foundation. Shared packages hold reusable contracts and domain logic. Nested tools support their owning app.

Each module card derives declared dependency and consumer links from package.json. The storefront domain guide links the existing runtime registries. Those two views cover different questions: package composition and public interfaces. Neither is a claim that every listed path executes in production.

## Record progress and keep the map current

1. Edit the relevant record in [catalog.json](catalog.json): purpose, scope, evidence, progress and next review. Update reviewedOn for a full inventory review; use explicit dates in progress for individual changes. Record completed checks and remaining work with evidence, without completion percentages.
2. Add new package or extension roots to modules. Add new storefront library or route-root directories to one storefrontDomains group; keep source paths in their existing locations.
3. Run `pnpm docs:modules` to regenerate these pages, then `pnpm audit:modules` to check coverage, evidence paths, declared dependencies and generated output. These commands use only local source files and Git filenames; they load no app code or credentials and make no network calls.
4. Run the checks appropriate to the code change and record their actual result. The map audit checks documentation structure; it does not run module tests, verify policy behavior or contact services.

The [catalog](catalog.json) is the authored record; Markdown cards are generated views. Existing app READMEs, [mission cards](../missions/README.md) and [handoffs](../handoffs/README.md) retain detailed plans and dated results. Link them instead of copying their task queues.

The coverage boundary is package/extension roots and immediate storefront domain directories. Nested implementation files are reached through those directories; this is not an exhaustive function inventory. Planned packages without source manifests remain in their original plans until implementation exists.
